title: The explicit trace discriminant section ideal commutes with localization to a basic open.
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite flat morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism] of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with $Y$ locally Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For every affine open $U$ and $r\in\Gamma(Y,U)$, extension of the explicit ideal $I_f(U)$ [def-sbc-trace-discriminant-section-ideal] along $\Gamma(Y,U)\to\Gamma(Y,D(r))$ equals $I_f(D(r))$.

proof.text: At every point of D(r), choose a free affine subchart V inside D(r) by the finite-flat affine-basis theorem and localization of a basis to a common principal refinement. This uses Module.Basis.localizationLocalization and exists_basicOpen_le_affine_inter.

For both U and D(r), the extension of the explicit section ideal to the stalk at this point equals the principal ideal of the germ of the supplied discriminant on V. The forward inclusion is a single test of the defining intersection, using Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap and germ_res. The reverse inclusion is precisely local generator membership.

Use IsAffineOpen.ideal_ext_iff on D(r). Rewrite the composite restriction and germ map using TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res, and identify both stalk ideals with the same local principal ideal. This proves localization, including empty D(r) vacuously.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BVH; stalkwise reduction using the explicit intersection construction
